content.comment_body: Hello. I'm new to this and would like advice on connecting a hall sensor to a [product_name] ([version_no]). In my scenario, [product_name] has a 24V DC power supply. The hall sensor operates simply - it conducts when an item is near and stops conducting when the item moves away. 1) The [product_name] requires 'up to 10VDC', which seems uncommon. More typical values are 5VDC and 12VDC, though 12VDC isn't allowed. Is it possible to use a 5VDC power supply instead? 2) Where should the ground from the 5VDC power supply (on the 5V side) be connected?

Hello [user_name], From your description, it sounds like your sensor board is designed for platforms like Raspberry Pi or Arduino. To connect this type of sensor to a [product_name], you would need to build an adjustment circuit. However, getting a sensor that's specifically compatible with [product_name] would be a more straightforward approach. Regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)
Do you have a datasheet or a link to the datasheet for your sensor?
[url] I just noticed it's actually called a Reed Switch. [url] Thank you, [user_name]
If you check the datasheet: The reed switch can operate with up to 100VDC. You can connect one terminal to +24VDC and the other to one of the input channels (I1 to I8) on [product_name].
NO means 'normally open' (magnet not near the reed switch), and it closes when the magnet gets close. NC means 'normally closed' (magnet not near), and it opens when the magnet approaches.
I have one more question. The manual mentions 'up to 10VDC.' Why is that? On page 330: Range 0VDC to 10VDC, Input impedance 80kΩ.

The 10VDC value doesn't refer to the digital inputs, but to the analog inputs. Inputs I1, I2, I7, and I8 can work as either digital or analog. The analog function handles signals from 0VDC to 10VDC, treating anything higher as 10VDC.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members discussed connecting a hall sensor, later clarified as a reed switch, to a [product_name] ([version_no]). The main points of confusion were around appropriate input voltage levels for different input types (analog versus digital), proper sensor selection, and correct wiring. Users encountered unclear documentation regarding safe voltage levels for connections.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking precise instructions on which input voltages are compatible and clear connection methods for low-voltage sensors with [product_name]. Additional clarification about the documentation's explanation of digital and analog input types is expected.
